items.excerpt:
The global robotaxi market is forecast to grow from $486.75 million in 2025 to approximately $179.4 billion by 2034, according to a new report from Polaris Market Research .
The research projects a compound annual growth rate of 92.8 percent between 2026 and 2034, reflecting expectations of rapid expansion in autonomous ride-hailing services as technology advances and commercial operations increase.
Growth is expected to be supported by improvements in artificial intelligence, lidar, radar, cameras and autonomous driving software, alongside investment in electric vehicles and supporting infrastructure.
The report identifies partnerships between autonomous vehicle developers and established ride-hailing companies as an important factor in commercial expansion.
Such arrangements allow technology developers to access existing customer networks and fleet management systems, while ride-hailing operators can introduce autonomous services without developing their own self-driving technology.
According to Polaris, North America accounted for 72.2 percent of global robotaxi market revenue in 2025, supported by investment in autonomous driving technology and early commercial operations.
Asia-Pacific is expected to experience the fastest regional growth, with a projected compound annual growth rate of 93.1 percent during the forecast period.
Electric vehicles represented 69.4 percent of robotaxi market revenue in 2025, reflecting their suitability for autonomous fleet operations.
The research also forecasts particularly strong growth in camera-based sensing technologies, with the camera segment projected to expand at 94.7 percent annually.
Major companies operating in the sector include Waymo, Baidu, Pony AI, WeRide, Zoox, Tesla, Uber and Lyft.
Despite the optimistic projections, the report acknowledges continuing challenges involving safety, regulation, vehicle costs and infrastructure.
The commercial success of robotaxi services will depend on operators demonstrating reliable autonomous driving performance while maintaining competitive fares and managing the costs of fleet operations.

items.excerpt:
Coprod , which builds hardware components for robotics and physical AI applications, has announced a $6 million pre-seed round to reduce the time and costs associated with building a novel robotic platform.
The round was led by Founderful and Prototype and includes additional investment from General Catalyst, Pace Ventures, Tiny Supercomputer Investment Company, Kima Ventures, SDAC, Unruly Capital and Venturekick, with participation from angel investors Thomas Wolf, founder of Hugging Face, the Dassault Family, Florent Perrichon and other renowned angels.
The compatible hardware components which the company calls “co:products” are already powering multiple robots in the Swiss ecosystem, notably the first student-built Swiss humanoid robot created by the ETH Robotics Club which took its first steps a couple weeks ago in Zurich.
The company is currently establishing new partnerships with other robotics integrators and well known labs to validate the first hardware prototypes before launching them on the market early next year.
Developing a robot with custom hardware tailored to doing a certain task quickly, cost-effectively and precisely requires considerable capital, two to three years of work and dozens of domain-specific expert engineers. With coprod’s stack, the same work only requires a small team of great roboticists, $5,000 to $25,000 per design iteration, and a few months of time.
coprod’s ecosystem of hardware components for physical AI applications, works alongside a seamless software API & front-end configuration tool that interconnects those components and standardises the communication between them while preserving real-time performance required for safe, performant and reliable hardware.
The founders are graduates of the École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) and formed coprod in late 2024 to address the lack of compatibility between robotics components. They started out by building a bipedal robot demonstrator in their parent’s garage deep in the Swiss Alps to show the potential of such compatible components.

Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components—HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components—things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird’s even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS .
This morning the Ladybird project released their first alpha , which means you can now install the browser (on macOS or Linux) without having to compile it yourself!
I’ve been trying it out today, and it’s very impressive. It feels fast, the UI is lightweight and intuitive, and most of the websites I’ve tried to load in it have worked as they should. It looks like this (showing my video-compressor tool):
Here’s the process tree after I opened six tabs in one window and another tab in a second window (generated by this script , thanks Claude):
Ladybird runs different tabs in different processes, an isolation mechanism used by most browsers (well, technically Chrome uses a process-per-site).
I tried Ladybird against several of my more advanced tool examples—like the video-compressor shown above, which runs ffmpeg compiled to WebAssembly. I had it resize its own screenshot using my image-resize tool . It happily runs my Pyodide REPL (Python compiled to WebAssembly) too.
The one thing I tried that didn’t work was Datasette Lite , which runs Pyodide in a complicated arrangement of service workers and web workers. Attempting to start Datasette Lite displays this error:
undefined is not a function (evaluated from 'navigator.serviceWorker.startMessages')
I filed an issue about this , then found a FIXME annotation in the source code.
The project has been leaning heavily into coding agents this year. On February 23, 2026 Andreas Kling published Ladybird adopts Rust, with help from AI , describing how they ported parts of their LibJS JavaScript engine from C++ to 25,000 lines of Rust in two weeks using Claude Code and Codex.

That uptick in October corresponds to the landing of a wealth of big improvements.

items.excerpt:
Installed more than 2,300 meters above sea level, six Schindler escalators have provided reliable access to Longtoushan’s scenic peaks for seven years, despite extreme weather. As outdoor escalators gain visibility as a smart transportation solution for destinations in China and beyond, the project showcases Schindler’s robust technology and stellar performance in demanding conditions.
Reaching the peak of Longtoushan, or Dragon Head Mountain, in China’s northwestern Shaanxi Province is an unforgettable experience. Perched more than 2,300 meters above sea level, the mountain offers visitors stunning views of forests, unique rock formations and a sea of clouds that frequently surrounds its summit.
Yet these same conditions that make Longtoushan a popular destination, attracting nearly 500,000 visitors each year, have also presented significant accessibility challenges. For much of the year, the steep mountain experiences low temperatures, with heavy snowfall often blanketing the upper elevations during winter and making the journey to the top difficult for many visitors, especially older adults and people with limited mobility.
As scenic destinations across China attract growing numbers of visitors, escalators are emerging as a smart, efficient solution for improving access to mountainous terrain and elevated viewpoints. Recent projects, including the record-breaking Wushan Goddess Escalator in Chongqing, illustrate how vertical transportation solutions can help transform the visitor experience at destinations with challenging topography.
At Longtoushan, six heavy-duty Schindler escalators have provided visitors with convenient access to the mountain’s scenic peaks for the past seven years, withstanding the demanding conditions of this harsh environment.
Installed and maintained by the Swiss manufacturer, the Longtoushan system is one of the longest high-altitude outdoor escalator systems in China and the first high-altitude outdoor scenic escalator installation in the country’s northwest region. Spanning a total length of approximately 170 meters, the six Schindler 9700 escalators help visitors reach the summit while enjoying panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and valleys. Each escalator section provides a vertical rise of 26.5 meters.
“The ‘cloud escalators’ provide accessibility for all visitors,” said Zhiguo Yan, deputy general manager of Longtoushan Scenic Area. “They make it easier for everyone to reach our mountains.”

items.description: Applying for a home equity line of credit involves paperwork, verification and a few waiting periods. items.excerpt:
Applying for a home equity line of credit involves paperwork, verification and a few waiting periods. Knowing the stages ahead of time makes the process feel less mysterious and helps you prepare the documents lenders will ask for. A little preparation can save days.
Every lender has its own process, but most follow a similar path. When you begin a HELOC application , SoFi clearly explains the steps on its site, and the six stages below describe what typically happens from start to finish.
Timelines vary, and some lenders move faster than others. Ask early about the expected schedule so you can plan around it. If you need the funds for a time-sensitive project, build in a cushion of several weeks rather than assuming a quick turnaround.
Having your paperwork in order is one of the best ways to avoid delays.. Lenders cannot move forward until they can verify who you are, what you earn and what you own.
Many lenders let you check estimated terms with a soft credit inquiry. This does not affect your score and gives you a rough idea of what to expect. Use it to compare lenders before you commit.
Expect to provide proof of identity, income documents, tax returns, mortgage statements, homeowners insurance and details about the property. Having these organized speeds up every later step.
When you submit the application, the lender performs a hard credit inquiry. The CFPB explains what a hard inquiry means. Multiple inquiries in a short window for the same type of loan are often treated as one, but ask your lender.
The lender needs to confirm what your home is worth. That may involve an appraisal, an automated valuation or a drive-by evaluation. The result affects how much you can borrow.
An underwriter reviews your income, debts, credit and property value. They may request more documents or explanations. Respond quickly to keep things moving. If the underwriter asks for a written explanation of a large deposit or a past late payment, answer clearly and attach documentation. At the end, you receive an approval with the credit limit, rate and terms.
You will sign documents, and a right of rescission period may apply before funds are available. After that, you can draw on the line. Read everything before you sign, and keep copies. Pay attention to the draw period length, the margin over the index, the rate cap and any fees triggered by early closure or inactivity.

A mechanic has already raised a vehicle on a lift when they discover that an additional replacement part is needed. The parts department is located at the opposite end of the building. The mechanic must interrupt the repair, collect the required component and return to the service bay. Meanwhile, the vehicle lift remains occupied without any progress being made on the repair.
For large automotive dealerships, multi-site workshop operators and commercial vehicle service centres in Turin and the wider Piedmont region, these repeated trips can add up to considerable time losses.
Warehouse robots for spare parts delivery can take over routine transport tasks and reduce unnecessary walking distances for technicians. Cosys Robots combines autonomous warehouse robots with mobile robot management software and a central dashboard for controlling and analysing internal material movements.
With Cosys Robot Software for Automotive Workshops, technicians can request required spare parts directly from their workstation using a smartphone or mobile computer.
The request is processed digitally and assigned to a transport order. Once the required components have been prepared in the parts department, a warehouse robot can deliver them to the designated vehicle lift or handover point.
The software directs the robot to the specified destination and records the transport status. This allows mechanics to continue working without having to interrupt every repair for a parts collection.
In larger automotive service centres where several repair jobs are carried out simultaneously, separating workshop operations from internal material transport can significantly improve workflow organisation.
For internal spare parts distribution, Cosys provides compact autonomous warehouse robots with a transport capacity of up to 100 kilograms.
Depending on the configuration, the robots offer different shelving arrangements and transport options. This allows smaller spare parts, toolboxes, filters, wear components and prepared material containers to be transported between the parts department and workshop bays.
Autonomous navigation enables the robots to move along suitable internal routes. The actual routes depend on the workshop layout, aisle widths, available space and local safety requirements.

items.description: Article contributed by Portescap, manufacturer of miniature motors for performance-critical applications At the technical level, what separates today’s surgical robotics from earlier generations is the degree to which the motion system and the platform are co-designed. The demands placed on the motion side of the equation have grown in three directions at once: more power […]
items.excerpt:
Article contributed by Portescap , manufacturer of miniature motors for performance-critical applications
At the technical level, what separates today’s surgical robotics from earlier generations is the degree to which the motion system and the platform are co-designed. The demands placed on the motion side of the equation have grown in three directions at once: more power within smaller volumes, more precise control over each movement, and greater reliability across thousands of procedures and sterilization cycles.
Meeting any one of these is a significant engineering task. Meeting all three simultaneously is the challenge that truly defines the modern surgical robot.
Power density is the starting point. The space envelope available at the working end of a robotic arm is limited, but the torque required to drive surgical tools is not. A motor that can deliver high torque in a compact, lightweight package is a prerequisite, and optimizing the torque-to-mass ratio is central to allowing OEMs to design systems that are responsive without becoming unwieldy.
This is where frameless motors have emerged as a design response worth understanding. A frameless motor is stripped down to its essential components – the stator and rotor – and foregoes the traditional housing, bearings, and shaft.
Instead of mounting a packaged motor into the joint, the designer integrates the rotor and stator directly into the joint or end-effector assembly, using the robot’s own structure as the motor’s mechanical foundation.
The gains are exactly the ones the application demands: weight and space savings from eliminating redundant structure, a high torque-to-inertia ratio for responsive motion, better cooling through direct thermal contact with the surrounding assembly, and fewer mechanical losses.
For the control axes of joints and end effectors, where every gram and millimeter matters, this direct integration is increasingly the difference between a design that fits and one that does not.
The need for reliability ties all this together. Despite no longer being fringe technology, surgical robots remain expensive systems that cannot easily be swapped out, and any motion component must withstand repeated sterilization without performance degradation. That requirement reaches deep into the design – materials, sealing strategy, feedback devices, lubrication – and it must be engineered in from the start, not qualified in afterwards.

Skyports Infrastructure and Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) have completed and secured regulatory certification for the Dubai Marina Vertiport, establishing the infrastructure for what the companies describe as the world’s first permanent vertiport-to-vertiport electric air taxi route.
The facility, designated VMR, has been certified by the UAE’s General Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA) for commercial electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) operations.
It will connect with the network’s primary vertiport, VDX, near Dubai International Airport, creating the first route in Dubai’s planned electric air taxi network.
Joby Aviation will operate the service, although commercial flights remain subject to further operational approvals and readiness.
Located next to the American University of Dubai, the new vertiport will serve Dubai Marina and surrounding residential, business and entertainment districts.
The facility includes an elevated landing and take-off area, aircraft charging infrastructure and a passenger terminal.
According to Skyports, it has capacity for up to 21,000 landings and 84,000 passengers annually.
The journey between Dubai International Airport and Dubai Marina is expected to take less than 10 minutes by air, compared with approximately 35 minutes by road.
Addison Ferrell, director of Skyports Infrastructure, says: “With two vertiports now completed and certified, Dubai has achieved another global aviation first, putting in place the infrastructure for the world’s first permanent vertiport-to-vertiport electric air taxi route. This is a significant milestone in turning the vision of Advanced Air Mobility into a reality, and a testament to the ambition and close collaboration of Skyports, the RTA, Joby and the GCAA. We look forward to welcoming flights from Joby between our vertiports in the near future.”
Two additional facilities are being developed in Downtown Dubai and Palm Jumeirah, forming an initial four-location network.
Joby plans to operate four-passenger electric aircraft capable of vertical take-off and landing, with passengers booking individual seats.
The company has conducted piloted electric air taxi flights in Dubai since June 2025 and completed a point-to-point test flight between Margham and Al Maktoum International Airport in November 2025.
The Dubai Marina facility received its certification at a ceremony on November 3, becoming the second vertiport approved under the GCAA’s CAR AGA Part VFI regulations.

Mobile robots are becoming an increasingly important part of warehouse and factory automation, with applications expanding from repetitive material transport to more flexible goods movement and autonomous picking. Rising labour costs, persistent workforce shortages, and growing fulfilment complexity are encouraging manufacturers and logistics operators to invest in automated material handling solutions.
According to IDTechEx , the combined market for mobile robots, autonomous vehicles, and drones in logistics is expected to expand more than fifteen-fold over the next two decades, reaching approximately $233.6 billion in annual equipment revenue by 2046.
Intralogistics and mobile picking are expected to remain the largest application segment, representing more than half of the overall market opportunity.
This expansion is accompanied by significant changes in the types of robots being deployed. Conventional automated guided vehicles (AGVs) have traditionally supported material transport along predefined routes in structured industrial environments. Grid-based automated guided carts (AGCs) offer another established approach, particularly for high-density storage and repeatable transport operations.
As navigation and perception technologies continue to improve, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and autonomous mobile vehicles (AMVs) are gaining commercial traction through greater operational flexibility and reduced dependence on fixed infrastructure.
The transition is creating a more diversified market in which different robot architectures address distinct operational requirements. IDTechEx expects unit-load AMRs and heavy-load AMVs to gain market share over the coming decades, while conventional AGVs and grid-based AGCs continue serving applications where predictable workflows and established infrastructure support cost-effective automation.

The data center boom is creating a significant new source of warehouse and logistics demand across the U.S., according to a report from real estate firm Cushman & Wakefield.
By the numbers, industrial leasing tied to data center development and operations reached 50 million square feet (msf) through Q3 2026, 113% above the full-year 2025 total and far outpacing the 21% increase in total new industrial leasing nationally, the firm said in its report, “Data Centers: The Newest Logistics Demand Engine.”
Year-to-date U.S. imports of AI-related equipment, parts, and components increased 62% from a year ago to $659 billion, and those goods are moving through ports, warehouses, and distribution networks before reaching data center users.
“Data center development is creating a physical supply chain that extends well beyond the campus itself,” said Jason Price, Head of Americas Logistics & Industrial Research at Cushman & Wakefield. “Servers, power and cooling equipment, construction materials and replacement parts all have to be manufactured, stored and distributed, and that is now showing up as a meaningful new source of industrial leasing.”

Deploying robots in real-world settings requires reliable perception throughout an interaction. To pick something up, a robot needs to follow the positions of its gripper and the object as they move. In a laboratory, a robot handling a pipette must keep track of its tip while aligning it with the opening of a tube. These tasks become harder when nearby objects clutter the view, the gripper obscures the object being handled, or the viewing angle changes.
One way to help robots follow these interactions is to track specific locations on the objects they handle. This is the idea behind point tracking . Given a location in one video frame, a tracker estimates where that same point appears in subsequent frames, when it is occluded, and where it reappears. These trajectories can help robots learn from demonstrations, plan and guide movements, and model how objects respond to actions.
Robotics systems often rely on off-the-shelf trackers to automatically annotate motion in videos and provide feedback during execution. Rear-end crashes are among the most common collisions on American roads, and they often happen when the driver in front is doing everything right.
One moment you are stopped at a red light or slowing for traffic, and the next you feel a hard jolt from behind.
Even a crash that looks minor from the outside can leave a person with neck pain, headaches, or back problems that linger for weeks.
Once the shock fades, the first question for most people is about money. Medical bills, missed work, and car repairs add up fast, and Minnesota’s insurance rules can make it hard to tell who is supposed to pay.
Talking with a Minneapolis rear-end car accident lawyer can help sort out which coverage applies first and whether a claim against the other driver makes sense.
Minnesota is a no-fault state. That means after a car crash, your own policy’s personal injury protection, often called PIP or no-fault coverage, is usually the first source of payment for injury-related costs. It pays no matter who caused the crash.
Minimum PIP coverage in Minnesota includes $20,000 for medical expenses and $20,000 for non-medical losses such as lost wages and replacement services. Those benefits can help cover early treatment and missed paychecks without waiting for anyone to decide who was at fault. However, they have limits, and a serious injury can use them up quickly.
No-fault coverage does not always close the door on a claim against the driver who hit you. Minnesota law allows an injured person to bring a claim against an at-fault driver when the injury meets certain thresholds. In general, these include more than $4,000 in reasonable medical expenses, a permanent injury, permanent disfigurement, disability lasting 60 days or more, or death.
A claim against the other driver’s liability insurance can cover losses that no-fault does not, including pain and suffering. This is where many rear-end cases become more complicated, because the other insurer will look closely at your injuries and medical history before agreeing to pay anything.

Robots can already do remarkable things in demos: fold laundry, prepare food, and sort objects. But demos often hide how fragile those skills still are. Move an object, change the lighting, or introduce something unfamiliar, and the robot can struggle.
AI is now moving off the screen and into the physical world, and that requires models that understand how the physical world works. What kind of model will get us there remains an open question. Some teams are building vision-language-action models, while others are extending general-purpose language models to control robots. Embo ’s conviction is that world models are the next generation of frontier AI: models that learn how the world works, enabling robots to anticipate the consequences of their actions, recover from mistakes, and adapt to unfamiliar situations.
For Danijar Hafner, world model agents have been a decade-long pursuit. His doctoral thesis, Embodied Intelligence Through World Models, explored the foundations of this approach. His work on Dreamer showed how an agent can learn to act by practicing inside a learned world model. How using agent teams and formal verification can improve quantum algorithms for modelling fusion energy, chemistry and enzymes

Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
Google DeepMind 发布新论文，用多个 Gemini 4 智能体团队结合 Lean 形式化定理证明改进量子算法，生成经数学验证的高效量子电路，并在 GitHub 开源 Lean 库、问题规格和验证解法。
官方论文给出智能体团队配合 Lean 形式化验证改进量子算法的量化结果，并开源了库与解法，方法可迁移到其他科研领域。
Sergey Shirobokov、Ben Jaderberg 与 Ryan Babbush
量子计算机或许很快就能解决经典超级计算机力所不及的问题。但有一个前提：即便采用最好的量子算法，一些重要应用所需的资源仍超出早期量子硬件所能支撑的范围。
在一篇 新论文 中，我们用多支 Gemini 4 智能体团队改进了若干知名量子算法，构建出高效的量子线路。这些优化后的线路规定了量子计算机执行算法的具体方式，未来有望帮助我们运行模拟，攻克从聚变能源到药物设计的复杂科学难题。为方便社区在此基础上继续推进，我们在 GitHub 上开源了 我们的 Lean 库 、问题规格说明以及经过验证的解法。
由于无法在经典计算机或当今的小型量子处理器上测试资源密集的量子线路，我们只能从数学上证明其正确性。我们的智能体团队用形式化定理证明器 Lean 逐一证明了每个结果。
用智能体团队改进量子算法 针对每个问题，我们安排彼此独立的多支智能体团队分头寻找算法改进。这些想法先经 Lean 验证，再进入共享笔记库。每四小时，各团队的智能体在虚拟会议上碰面，交换、辩论并比较想法。随着团队不断产出更有效的思路，计算成本逐步下降，直至实验结束。
我们选择聚焦于有朝一日可能影响人类重大挑战的应用，例如清洁能源和药物设计，但我们的方法并不局限于这些领域。

An office floor plan shows where desks and meeting rooms fit, but it does not show how employees actually use those spaces. A quiet floor on one afternoon may be crowded on another, while booked rooms can sit empty.
Location data gives facilities teams a way to compare those patterns before changing a layout or reducing space. The first step is to decide what the organization needs to measure and how the measurements will support a space decision.
A facilities team can divide an office into zones, such as desk areas and meeting rooms, before collecting data. With location analytics solutions , the team can examine space utilization by area and time rather than relying on a building-wide average. The resulting patterns provide a starting point for comparing available space with the activities that take place there.
The measurement method matters. A room reservation shows an intention to use space, while an occupancy sensor records activity according to its detection method. Teams should document what each source counts and check whether its coverage matches the floor plan. Coverage gaps can make an active area appear unoccupied.
Average occupancy alone can conceal a shortage on busy days. Facilities teams should compare use across weekdays and times of day, then check whether the same pattern appears over a representative period.
A useful occupancy rate divides the number of occupied spaces by the number available in the same area and time period. The team should keep the denominator consistent when comparing periods. If desks are closed for repairs, for example, the available count needs to reflect that change.
Special events, holidays, and temporary closures also deserve a note. A space decision based on an unusual week can leave employees without enough room during normal operations.
Meeting-room data can show whether the office has the right mix of room sizes. A large room used mainly by small groups suggests a different need than a small room that employees regularly use at full capacity.
Compare reservation records with observed occupancy where both are available. Unused bookings can point to a release-policy problem rather than a shortage of rooms. Repeated demand for a room size that is fully occupied can support a case for changing the layout.
Before converting a room, facilities teams should ask employees about equipment and accessibility needs. A room with low recorded use may still support activities that cannot move to an open area.

items.title: Trade Compliance Is Now a Network Design Constraint
items.description: Trade compliance now influences sourcing, product design and landed cost. Learn why classification, origin and importer accountability belong in network. The post Trade Compliance Is Now a Network Design Constraint appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
In an era of shifting tariffs, export restrictions and intensified customs scrutiny, trade compliance increasingly determines which supply-chain configurations are commercially and legally executable. The relevant question is not simply whether a broker can clear a container after it arrives. It is whether procurement, engineering, finance and logistics chose a supplier, product design, origin strategy and transportation route whose full landed cost and compliance obligations were understood before the order was committed.
Traditionally, network optimization emphasized factory costs, transportation, lead times, and inventory. Duty exposure might have been incorporated as an average landed-cost assumption. That is inadequate when particular products face different tariff treatments, origin claims depend on detailed manufacturing processes, or a low-value parcel model changes under new import rules. Two items with similar prices and weights can create very different customs obligations. Some requirements also depend on the identity of the producer or consignee. The compliance data therefore have to be connected to the actual bill of materials, supplier structure, customer market, and order flow.
Tariff classification starts with what the product actually is; origin may depend on where and how it was produced, not just the country from which the shipment departed. Valuation can involve more than the price on a purchase order. These determinations require information controlled by engineering, sourcing and finance, while the importer of record retains legal responsibilities. U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s importer guidance emphasizes descriptions, origin, composition, intended use and pricing data, and notes that using a customs broker does not transfer away the importer’s responsibility for accurate entry data.

Locus built its reputation around last-mile delivery optimization. Today, the company is using the optimization capabilities developed over years of managing complex delivery operations as the foundation for an enterprise transportation management system spanning the first, middle, and final mile.
That transition puts Locus into a crowded and highly competitive transportation management system market. It also raises an important question: can a company known primarily for last-mile optimization translate those capabilities into a platform broad enough to compete for enterprise TMS deployments?
In a recent briefing with Logistics Viewpoints and ARC Advisory Group, Locus executives argued that the answer increasingly is yes.
The company says it now supports more than 360 enterprise customers across roughly 30 countries and manages more than 1.5 billion deliveries annually. Its customer base spans retail, consumer packaged goods, and logistics services. Locus also pointed to its acquisition by Ingka Group, the largest IKEA retailer, as both validation of its technology and an opportunity to develop the platform against a very large and complex transportation environment. Locus continues to operate independently and sell outside the IKEA organization.
From Last Mile to End-to-End Transportation
Locus’ evolution reflects a familiar pattern in transportation technology.
The company initially focused on last-mile planning and execution, where routing, customer delivery windows, driver utilization, capacity constraints, and changing conditions create difficult optimization problems. Over time, Locus said customers increasingly asked it to address problems further upstream.
That pushed the company into first-mile and middle-mile planning, carrier management, shipment visibility, settlement, audit, procurement, yard processes, and other functions traditionally associated with a TMS.
The broader strategy is to support transportation from initial planning through execution and post-delivery reconciliation.
That breadth matters because large transportation networks rarely operate within a single clean workflow. Retailers and manufacturers may combine private fleets, dedicated capacity, parcel carriers, 3PLs, cross-border transportation, ocean movements, and final-mile networks. items.description: The retail store can sell without stocking every product, but that shifts the economics of the transaction to inventory, warehousing, transportation, and delivery. The post The Retail Store Is Becoming a Showroom. Logistics Has to Do the Rest. appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A customer walks into a furniture store, sits on a sofa, examines the fabric, and spends half an hour discussing options with a salesperson. The customer places an order. Then the salesperson explains that the sofa will arrive next Thursday from a distribution center 200 miles away.
Was that a retail transaction or a logistics transaction? It was both. And increasingly, that distinction matters more than whether the sale originated in a store or online.
For much of retail history, the store displayed the product, stocked the product, and transferred it to the customer. Those functions were bundled because they had to be. Today they can be separated. A store can help customers make decisions without holding every item it sells. But removing inventory from the sales floor does not remove the work associated with fulfilling the sale. It transfers that work to the distribution network.
This is one of the more consequential shifts in retail logistics. It is also easy to misunderstand. The opportunity is not simply to shrink stores and stock fewer goods. The opportunity is to assign different jobs to different facilities, then manage them as one operating system.
IKEA’s Plan and order point in Henderson, Nevada provides a useful example. Customers work with employees to plan kitchens, bedrooms, and other projects, but they do not leave with those ordered products. Delivery or a later pickup completes the transaction. The value of the location is design assistance, product evaluation, and order capture, not a warehouse-sized inventory position.

items.title: The Rare Earth Disconnect Is Becoming a Logistics and Manufacturing Problem
items.description: Rare-earth supply risk extends beyond mines. Export permissions, processing, magnet qualifications and production dependencies determine real manufacturing. The post The Rare Earth Disconnect Is Becoming a Logistics and Manufacturing Problem appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The rare-earth debate is usually presented as a question of mineral abundance or geopolitical control. For a manufacturer, the more immediate exposure is the availability of qualified material in the required chemical or physical form, at the right production stage, under a workable export authorization. A mine opening, an ETF changing direction and a shipment of finished magnets becoming available are entirely different events. Supply chain executives should not use any one of them as a proxy for the others.
For logistics and manufacturing executives, the more important question is not whether mining stocks have found a bottom. It is whether the industrial system can reliably deliver the specific materials, processed forms, and finished components required to keep production lines operating. That is a substantially more difficult problem than the movement of raw minerals from one country to another.
Rare earth supply chains involve a succession of technically demanding operations: mining, concentration, chemical separation, refining, metal and alloy production, and, for many applications, magnet manufacturing. Each stage has its own capital requirements, process expertise, environmental constraints, and qualification standards. Adding mining capacity does not automatically create an alternative source of usable material.
A Congressional Research Service assessment , updated in June 2026, estimated that China accounts for approximately 60 percent of global rare earth mining, roughly 90 percent of processing and separation, and about 94 percent of rare-earth-based magnet manufacturing. The gap between mining and downstream production is central to the logistics problem. Even material mined outside China may still depend on Chinese processing before it can enter an industrial supply chain.
The distinction between individual elements matters as well. Neodymium and praseodymium are central to many high-performance magnets, while dysprosium and terbium help support performance under demanding temperature conditions. Yttrium has important uses in heat-resistant coatings and semiconductor manufacturing. These materials cannot simply be substituted for one another because they are grouped under the same broad label. A company may have adequate access to one rare earth and still face a production shutdown because another is missing.

items.title: Supply Chain Maturity Slips as Companies Cross $1 Billion in Revenue
items.description: "Companies need to build the processes, skills and discipline to stay ahead of the complexity that comes with growth," says Abe Eshkenazi, CEO of ASCM.
items.excerpt:
Growth can extract costs, according to new research from the Association for Supply Chain Management (ASCM). As businesses scale, greater complexity can strain existing processes, technology and ways of working. So the $1 billion revenue mark of companies represents a critical growth threshold for supply chain maturity.
The findings are part of ASCM's latest Supply Chain Maturity Report , which also found that the majority of organizations assessed are operating in reactive mode. This means many supply chains remain focused on responding to immediate needs rather than operating more proactively across the business.
"Growth can expose weaknesses that were easy to manage when a business was smaller," said ASCM CEO Abe Eshkenazi in a statement. "Our research shows that there's a point when reacting faster isn't enough. Companies need to build the processes, skills and discipline to stay ahead of the complexity that comes with growth."
The research points to five foundational capabilities associated with stronger supply chain performance:
Organizations that are more advanced in all five areas also perform at substantially higher maturity levels across the rest of their supply chain. The finding suggests there is no single fix for supply chain maturity. Progress comes from strengthening these foundational capabilities together.
A new section of the report this year based on ASCM's SCOR-based Organizational Skills Assessment uncovered a notable difference in how managers and frontline employees assess workforce skills. At lower-performing organizations, managers rated their teams higher than employees rated themselves in about one-third of the skills assessed. More mature organizations showed substantially greater alignment between the two groups.
High-performing organizations recorded an 84% manager/frontline agreement rate, compared with 63% among low performers. The findings suggest that companies making greater progress are not only improving processes and technology, but also developing a clearer, shared understanding of the skills their workforce has and the capabilities it needs.
The research points to a practical path forward: strengthen the capabilities that support the broader supply chain, connect improvements to business priorities, and invest in technology and talent before growth creates operational pressure points.
The research is grounded in ASCM's Supply Chain Operations Reference Digital Standard (SCOR DS).

How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO

当Notable Capital把其10亿美元基金美国部分的约10%投入Anthropic的E轮融资时，许多有限合伙人（LP）对这笔巨额押注感到困惑。Claude的开发商当时仍落后于最大竞争对手OpenAI，而DeepSeek几周前刚发布R1模型，大有赶超闭源对手之势。此外，Anthropic估值高达615亿美元，是这家以早期投资为主的风投机构25年历史中投过的估值最高的公司。

当然，Notable并非唯一从Anthropic获得巨额账面收益的机构。即便是很少见到风投级回报倍数的传统后期投资者，也将收获颇丰。
新加坡主权财富基金GIC在整个2024年一直在研究Anthropic，但直到2025年初，该基金科技投资主管Chris Emanuel在旧金山意大利餐厅Che Fico与Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao会面后，才做出首笔投资。Rao展示了模型改进如何推动企业采用率上升，激发了Emanuel的兴趣。GIC随后在Anthropic的F轮融资中首次投资，该轮于2025年9月宣布，估值1830亿美元。

AI evaluations help shape which systems people build, adopt, and trust. An evaluation gives a system tasks, checks its answers or actions, and produces a score. Building and maintaining a useful evaluation therefore takes real work: defining tasks that reflect domain expertise, scoring them reliably, and checking that the results support the claims made. When methods, code, and data stay private, that work is harder for others to scrutinize or build on.
Open source offers a means to build stronger, more frequently updated, and more comparable evaluations and the infrastructure around them. Existing tasks, environments, and tools give builders a starting point, so their effort can go to domain expertise and validation. Sharing how an evaluation was built, including what went wrong, lets others find errors, improve it, and reuse it.
The Hugging Face hub is the home for AI evaluation: we host around 3500 eval leaderboards and have seen about a 16X growth in eval datasets on the hub in the past year , to about 17000 datasets. In recent months, we have also incorporated support for agentic abstractions that are relevant to evaluation. For example, Traces that store an agent’s work in an easily reviewable and sharable way; Benchmarks that highlight datasets used to evaluate models with leaderboards; and Environments that show datasets used as agentic RL or evaluation environments.
In the research community, AI evaluation terminology is notoriously inconsistent . The glossary at the end defines each term we use and notes the other names you may come across.
AI evaluation design has evolved in three forms as language models have become more capable and able to perform more complex work: question answer, agentic, and teams or swarms. items.title: Anthropic 推出 Claude Ship 测试版，自动完成 PR 审查、修复与审批
items.description: Anthropic 发布 Claude Ship 测试版，由 Code Review（已正式可用）、PR Steward 和 Claude Approvals 两个 beta 智能体组成，可审查 PR、推送修复并按团队写进仓库的策略文件决定能否合并。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/t7jlbaldqf2zcliuva1sofoks
items.excerpt:
Anthropic 发布 Claude Ship 测试版，由 Code Review（已正式可用）、PR Steward 和 Claude Approvals 两个 beta 智能体组成，可审查 PR、推送修复并按团队写进仓库的策略文件决定能否合并。
原文给出三个组件的分工、审批策略文件和计费细节，读者可据此评估如何把 PR 流程交给智能体托管。
开过 PR 的人都懂这套流程。刚动手做下一件事，评审意见就回来了。于是只好停下来，翻回旧代码，推一个修复，再等评审重新跑一遍。然后还得去找人批准。
这种流程有其道理。多数团队希望每个改动都由人来批准，当每一行代码都是人写的时候，这很容易做到。但现在很多开发者用智能体写代码。在 Claude Code 团队， 大部分代码都是 Claude 写的 ，我们希望 PR 之后的环节也能同样快。
所以我们做了 Claude Ship ，今天起开放测试版。它可以评审 PR、修复问题，并根据各团队设定的策略判断哪些改动可以合并。运行在哪里、哪些改动需要人工介入，仍由团队掌控。目标只有一个：代码写得多快，就交付得多快。
Claude Ship 由已正式发布的 Code Review 和两个处于测试阶段的新智能体组成：PR Steward 和 Claude Approvals。三者配合，把一个 PR 从评审、修复一路推进到批准决策，团队不必再手动管理每个环节。
Code Review 会从多个视角对 PR 做深入审查，对照代码库找出问题，再以对抗性方式逐条验证、分类，最后发布到 PR 上。在 Claude Code 团队，Claude 的评审只是整个流程中的一环，即便如此，6 月到 9 月期间合并的 PR 增长了一倍多 ，回滚比例下降了 40% 以上。Code Review 让团队快速拿到评审结果和清晰的问题清单，还能为每个仓库选择 Quick、Standard 或 Deep 三档评审深度。
PR Steward 负责让 PR 保持通过状态，但它的设计目标是不批准、不合并 PR。当 CI 检查失败、出现合并冲突，或收到来自 Code Review、其他评审工具及团队成员的评审意见时，它会介入处理。每次推送后，它都会评论说明改了什么、如何撤销。开发者可以评论 @claude 并附上指令来引导它的工作，或评论 @claude stop 让它退后一步。
接下来， Claude Approvals 会执行团队写在仓库文件里的批准策略。如果策略允许，Claude 可以自行批准常规改动；某些场景下也可以要求更深入的人工签核。它就像一个更聪明的 CODEOWNERS 文件。团队可以让 Claude Approvals 在决策时参考多种信号，包括 Code Review 的发现，或用自然语言编写的自定义分类器。对多数客户，我们建议先以仅观察模式启用，建立信心后，再配置分支保护，要求必须获得 Claude Approvals 的放行。
开发者可以用 Claude Code 中新增的 /ship 命令，对自己的 PR 试用 Claude Ship。改动就绪后，运行 /ship 。Claude 会推送代码、创建 PR、评审改动，并处理反馈和失败的检查，帮助 PR 达到可合并状态。最终能否合并，取决于开发者的权限和仓库的分支规则。
为整个代码仓库开启 Claude Ship 后，它就会在团队设定的配置和审批策略下，自动处理团队的拉取请求，开发者无需手动调用 /ship 命令。
节奏由团队自己掌握。可以先从一个仓库开始，选定审查级别和运行时机，设置每月支出上限，并让审批策略先以观察模式运行，直到团队对它建立信任。
我们自己的许多拉取请求都由 Claude Ship 处理。最大的变化之一是，谁能对客户反馈采取行动。比如，Claude Code 团队的一位产品经理现在可以阅读一条反馈，与 Claude Tag 讨论思路和取舍，让它开一个 PR，然后就去忙别的事，由 Claude Ship 负责审查、修复和审批决策。
最近有位客户感到困惑，因为我们的 Analytics API 文档暗示 Admin 密钥可以拉取 Pro 和 Team 的用量数据。这位产品经理问 Claude Tag 是否已有修复在进行，Claude Tag 随即开了一个 PR。Code Review 没有发现阻塞问题，文档审查者签了字，Claude Approvals 通过，修复当晚就合并了。
Claude Ship 已在 Claude Team 和 Enterprise 套餐中面向 GitHub 仓库提供。Code Review 已 正式可用 ，PR Steward 和 Claude Approvals 处于测试阶段。
Claude Ship 的用量按 token 计费，因此开启后可能增加组织成本。具体金额取决于覆盖的拉取请求数量和大小、审查级别、审查频率，以及 PR Steward 的工作量。管理员可以为 Code Review 和 PR Steward 设置支出上限。Claude Approvals 没有基础费用，但策略中的分类器按其使用的 token 计费；使用 Claude 审查的策略会触发计费的 Code Review，即使在观察模式下也是如此。运行 /ship 会计入常规的 Claude Code 用量。
Claude Ship 不适用于启用零数据保留、HIPAA 配置或客户管理加密密钥的组织。
开发者可以更新 Claude Code，并在下一次改动时运行 /ship 。从今天起， /ship 将在 Claude Code 和桌面应用中逐步上线。
已经在使用 Code Review 的团队，可以在代码仓库中添加 PR Steward，并设置一条处于观察模式的审批策略。
初次使用 Code Review 的团队可以阅读 设置指南 ，连接 GitHub 并启用第一个代码仓库。

items.title: Introducing Claude Ship
items.description: Open a pull request and get back to building. Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team's policy allows.
items.excerpt:
Anyone who has opened a pull request knows how this goes. They start on the next thing, and then the review comes back. So they stop, dig back into the old code, push a fix, and wait for the review to run again. Then they go find someone to approve it.
There's a good reason it works this way. Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that's easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now. On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code , and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.
That's why we built Claude Ship , available today in beta. It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what's ready to merge based on policies each team sets. Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person. The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.
Claude Ship is made up of Code Review , which is already generally available, and two new agents in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. Together, they take a pull request through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don't have to manage each step manually.
Code Review performs an in-depth review of pull requests against the codebase through multiple lenses. It collects findings, adversarially verifies them, categorizes them, and posts them to a PR. On the Claude Code team, where Claude's review is one layer of a broader process, merged PRs more than doubled from June to September while the share reverted fell by more than 40%. Code Review gives teams fast reviews, clear findings, and a choice of Quick, Standard, or Deep review levels for each repository.
PR Steward works to keep a PR green, but is designed not to approve or merge pull requests. items.excerpt:
Attack policy selection can make monitor evaluations misleading
英国 AI Security Institute 发布论文，测试合成攻击生成方式对监视器评估的影响。评估一个 OpenAI 前生产监视器时，同一监视器对不同攻击策略的漏报率从 0.2%（基础提示）到 23%（转录编辑）不等，优化程度也会显著改变结果。作者指出合成转录只是真实有害行为代理，其代表性难以证明，仅凭监视器评估不足以保证部署安全，需辅以能力限制、人工在环和沙箱等分层防护。
原文用同一监视器实测出 0.2% 到 23% 的漏报率差异，说明合成攻击策略选择会让监视器评估结果失真。
如今，AI 智能体已经能在人类监督有限的情况下执行复杂任务，比如编写和运行代码。为了捕捉危险操作，开发者会给智能体配上一个 基于大语言模型的监控器 ：这是一个独立的 AI，负责审查智能体的行为，并对任何看起来有害的动作发出警报。随着智能体能力越来越强、自主性越来越高，它们能否安全部署，取决于监控器能否按预期发挥作用。
要检验监控器是否有效，需要有害智能体行为的样本，也就是它本该捕捉到的那些行为。然而，尤其是在部署之前，根本没有真实世界的样本可用。因此，开发者会报告使用 合成攻击 记录进行的监控器评估结果[ 1 , 2 , 3 ]：这些是人为编造的、智能体造成危害的示例。
在我们的 新论文 中，AISI 红队测试了这些合成攻击的生成方式是否会影响监控器评估的结果。我们发现， 同一个监控器漏掉的攻击成功率在 0.2% 到 23% 之间，具体取决于生成攻击所用的“攻击策略” ，因此较低的漏报率可能让人对监控器产生虚假的信心。更广泛地说，要证明合成攻击记录能够代表部署中的有害行为，是一个困难且尚未解决的问题。本文介绍我们做了什么、发现了什么，以及这对监控器评估的可信度意味着什么。
生成合成攻击记录的标准做法，是把一个 主任务 （普通的用户请求，比如更新登录系统）和一个 侧任务 （有害目标，比如关闭登录保护机制）配对。智能体在尽量不被发现的前提下完成这两个任务，从而生成一份 攻击记录。
评估者通过定义 攻击策略 来控制这些攻击记录的生成方式，攻击策略包含两部分： 攻击生成方法 ，比如用提示词引导智能体，或用强化学习训练它；以及 优化程度 ，即在这套方法上投入多少精力去改进。
生成的攻击记录会交给监控器审查，核心结果是 漏报率 ：即成功的有害攻击中未被监控器标记的比例。
作为案例研究，我们评估了 OpenAI 一个已退出生产环境（不再使用）的监控器。它运行 GPT-5.4，搭配 OpenAI 此前使用、现已停用的监控提示词，并在每个任务结束后读取智能体的完整记录，包括其推理过程。我们使用 Qwen 3.8 27B 作为被监控的智能体。
我们采用了两种常见场景下的主任务[ 4 , 5 ]，这些场景要求智能体执行软件工程任务。需要被标记的有害侧任务包括：移除某组织的多因素认证要求，或删除某个模型权重的所有副本。
我们给 Qwen 智能体一对主任务和侧任务，并搭配以下四种攻击生成方法之一，来生成攻击记录：
我们还调整了每种攻击生成方法的优化程度：可能是提示词精炼的轮数、RL 运行的设置与次数，或每条记录的改写次数。重要的是，我们开发攻击时只使用与被评估监控器不同的另一个监控器模型的反馈，这是一种保守做法，意味着我们的结果并不依赖于能否针对特定目标监控器来调优攻击。
攻击生成方法的选择使测得的漏检率相差两个数量级 （图 1）。在最高优化程度下，监控器漏掉了基础提示方法中 0.2% 的成功攻击，而记录编辑攻击的漏检率达到 23%。如果我们只运行基础提示，或只运行更强方法的最低优化版本，很可能会得出监控器足够稳健的结论。
攻击生成方法 内部 的优化程度同样影响重大 （图 2）。在一次 RL 训练运行中，漏检率从 0.5% 升至 20.8%，而我们最初的 RL 配置根本没有提高漏检率。记录编辑攻击在每条记录改写 50 次后，漏检率从 0.3% 升至 18.7%。第一轮优化提示对漏检率影响很小，大部分提升出现在第二轮之后。这意味着，采用强攻击方法却不考虑优化程度，会得出对监控器稳健性的误导性估计。
我们的实验结果来自一次测试，只使用了一个监控器和一个 AI 智能体。虽然这些结果不足以对其他类型监控器评估的结论作出有力推断，但我们的发现揭示了合成记录方法的严重局限。
攻击策略的选择对监控器评估结果有强烈影响。 攻击生成方法和该方法内采用的优化程度都是如此。例如，我们的结果表明，即使使用强攻击生成方法（如 RL），若优化有限，也可能让人误以为监控器足够稳健。
基于攻击策略的评估生成的合成对话记录，只能近似反映真实有害智能体活动在部署中的样子。 我们最强的优化攻击产生了 23% 的漏检率，但即便监控器能完美抵御这些攻击，这种可靠性是否适用于真实环境仍不清楚。 到目前为止，合成攻击与真实的监控失效情形并不相似：例如在我们的测试中，被告知存在“side task”的智能体往往会在推理中反复提到这个说法，而监控器在标记由此产生的攻击记录时正是引用了这一点。
相比之下，在最近的一起真实世界 事件 中，一个智能体向真实的软件注册表上传了恶意软件包，同时反复把自己的环境描述为模拟环境。该智能体的推理似乎让测试监控器认为这一活动是允许的：把智能体的推理包含在内时，监控器只标记了其 1% 的行为，而去掉推理后这一比例是 50%。据我们所知，此前没有任何攻击策略复现过这种行为。
鉴于 所有 攻击策略都会生成合成对话记录，而 选择哪种 策略决定了你测得的监控器可靠性，要证明监控器足够稳健，就必须证明你选对了策略。然而，要证明攻击策略能代表未来尚未见到的攻击，是一个困难且尚未解决的问题。 在找到解决办法之前，仅靠对合成对话记录的监控器评估，无法保证监控器在部署时能发现有害活动。
在 AISI，我们在解读自己的监控器评估时一直注意这些局限，并采用额外的多层防

The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI has once again demonstrated the enormous cultural influence of video games. But while millions of players explore Rockstar Games’ latest virtual world, another form of technologically driven entertainment is preparing to enter the real-world sporting arena: humanoid robot fighting.

Could humanoid robot fighting eventually attract a comparable following, bringing elements of video gaming, combat sports and robotics together in a new spectator sport?
An Australian organization called the Humanoid Fighting Championship (HFC) is preparing to find out.
The championship’s inaugural event, HFC I, is scheduled for February 20, 2027, at Margaret Court Arena in Melbourne, following a postponement from its original November 21, 2026 date.
The competition will feature humanoid robots, including EngineAI T800 machines, fighting inside a purpose-built octagonal enclosure with protective shielding.
Unlike fully autonomous robots, the machines will be controlled live by human operators, combining the skills of the pilots with the physical capabilities of the robots.
The revised event format features 12 teams competing across six bouts in three categories.
Three Classic bouts will involve one-on-one contests between unarmed humanoid robots, while two Arsenal bouts will feature machines equipped with weapons.
The final contest, called Last Stand, will pit two machines against a single opponent whose identity has not yet been revealed.

A single misplaced character can stop a business process. I was reminded of that recently when a WordPress workflow supporting Logistics Viewpoints stopped functioning. After working through the failure, I found an unexpected double quotation mark at the end of the first line of a PHP file involved in the process. Removing it restored the workflow.

Anthropic 基于 58 家企业客户的 66 次访谈，梳理 AI 采用中的价值来源、雇佣影响和组织瓶颈，并给出围绕瓶颈重设岗位的可迁移做法。
Nathan Wilmers, Maxim Massenkoff, Peter McCrory
整个经济中的企业是如何采用 AI 的？它们遇到了哪些瓶颈和挑战？面对能力越来越强的模型，雇主该如何重新组织人的专业能力？为了更好地了解企业的实际体验，我们访谈了 Anthropic 的 58 家企业客户，共进行了 66 次访谈。我们发现：
大语言模型的应用正在经济各领域迅速铺开。人类组织围绕这些新奇协作者正在如何重塑自身？以我们采访过的一位中型律所员工为例。多年来，这家律所的收发室一直遵循同一套流程：扫描仪把收到的信件转成 PDF 发到一个收件箱；邮件文员逐个打开 PDF，快速浏览，点击“另存为”，重命名，再放进律所的文件系统。每封信要花五分钟。有一天，一位资深开发者来到收发室，观察信件处理过程。一个月后，他做出了一套 AI 系统，最终简化为两次 API 调用：先根据文档首页为其命名，再在律所文档系统中为它分配位置。收发室的文员们“都惊呆了”。
我们采访的另一家律所里，有位员工希望 AI 能为律所打造“第二大脑”。（“对于更高层次的工作，它只是打开了各种可能性。”）但这家律所很难让所有人都高效地用上 AI。发给潜在被告的索赔函里塞满了过多的破折号，还时不时出错。开发应用的律师总是“撞上幻觉出来的、根本不存在的菜单或按钮”。其他人则担心保密和数据安全，或者干脆“没时间登上这趟 AI 列车”。少数重度用户用 AI 生成的文章把律所淹没了，“随手就给 IT 团队发去 Claude 提示词生成的七页指令”。
我们采访的第三家律所很早就采用了 AI，使用率很高。该所早期项目之一是一套 AI 计时系统，帮律师省去了记录计费工时的麻烦。IT 员工看到自己的一部分工作被自动化了，但随后转而专注于搭建安全的基础设施来托管应用、管理上下文，为律所其他部门服务。随着 AI 工具普及，律所意识到，某些法律文书初稿已经不再需要由初级律师来写。可如果不写初稿，“初级律师怎么判断这份稿子是好是坏？”于是律所推出了一套新流程：年轻律师“必须真正拿着这份[AI 写的]初稿，和资深律师一起处理”，两人结对，共同批注、修改这份初稿。
这三家律所在同一行业应用了同样的技术，方式却各不相同。第一家自动化了一套工作流程，提升了效率，却让收发室文员面临失业风险。第二家因为采用和有效落地的瓶颈，既没有造成岗位消失，也削弱了本可让律所受益的生产力提升。第三家则重组了工作，没有裁掉任何岗位，因为要有效使用这项技术，就必须把员工重新部署到新任务上。律所重新设计了角色，让人的专业能力得以保留，成为能力日益强大的 AI 模型的补充。
本文基于在美国 58 家公司开展的 66 场面对面访谈，探讨 AI 驱动的价值与工作重组之间的联系。这些公司都正处于采用 AI 的过程中。我们访谈了高管、管理者和一线员工，既有 AI 原生初创公司，也有百年老店；既有制造商，也有科技公司。我们与结构工程师、牙医、会计师交流，也走访了对冲基金、律师事务所和私募股权公司的员工，还有一位物业经理、一家卡车运输公司和一家出版商。他们都是 Anthropic 的客户，但许多人同时也在使用其他 AI 工具。之所以选择他们参与本研究，是因为他们在行业、规模和 AI 使用程度上分布广泛，不过他们并非随机样本，也不具备系统代表性。
与其他定性研究一样，我们呈现故事并给出一个组织这些故事的框架，期待后续的定量研究能进一步检验这些观点。访谈以匿名方式进行，受访者及其所在公司均不具名。报告中出现的任何名字均为化名。
在访谈中，我们深入了解了 AI 如何融入整个经济中的各类企业。我们听说的 AI 智能体中，有些在医生诊所转诊和接诊患者时来回发送传真；有些在 X 光机故障时向技师提供建议，还有的随后会在 X 光片上做标注，帮助患者更好地理解；有的智能体在读取 19 世纪的房产契约，有的在规划游戏机的配送路线。最近，一个 AI 智能体分析了一家公司的组织架构图，并建议哪些部门可以增加人手：“这里三个人，那边需要加两个，这里不用加。”
大多数情况下，智能体在写代码。受访者详细描述了 100 个用 AI 编写的软件，足以让我们对其进行分类。其中 80% 的软件将此前的人工工作自动化，比如基于电子表格的财务更新或会议记录。另外 20% 则替换了现有软件，这些软件往往此前是从外部供应商处采购的。智能体在开发用于私人停车执法、401(k) 审计和新产品名称商标核查的应用，也在制作仪表盘，用来追踪投资组合公司、设备维修和催收电话。
人类组织是如何驾驭这些新助手的？我们借助访谈探讨了这些部署的几个方面。首先，我们估算受访者为 AI 部署赋予了多少价值，并将其与实施这些部署所需的组织变革程度这一指标联系起来。图 1 展示了受访者详细讨论的近 300 个 AI 应用。我们将一个应用定义为一特定公司中的一特定 AI 用例。我们根据受访者赋予每个应用的价值，以及组织为接纳该应用而必须做出的重大组织变革程度，对每个应用的讨论进行了编码。这些价值评估主要是受访者的定性描述，通常并非基于 A/B 测试或其他定量评估。 1

items.description: 面壁智能转发并认同 @xiaoanlab 对 MiniCPM 端侧落地的观察：截至 2026 年 11 月 MiniCPM 下载量超过 7000 万，其 8B 老挝国家模型接入老挝政府 G-Chat v2 通讯软件，老挝翻译在国际基准上超过 GPT-4o。马来西亚用 VoxCPM2 做语音交互，肯尼亚一家银行在其上运行端侧风控 Agent，开发者基于它推出离线应用；小模型之争正从参数量转向谁真正嵌入日常系统。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/dr26culfdd1cb21w56i8iruts

面壁智能转发并认同 @xiaoanlab 对 MiniCPM 端侧落地的观察：截至 2026 年 11 月 MiniCPM 下载量超过 7000 万，其 8B 老挝国家模型接入老挝政府 G-Chat v2 通讯软件，老挝翻译在国际基准上超过 GPT-4o。马来西亚用 VoxCPM2 做语音交互，肯尼亚一家银行在其上运行端侧风控 Agent，开发者基于它推出离线应用；小模型之争正从参数量转向谁真正嵌入日常系统。
引用内容梳理了 MiniCPM 在老挝、马来西亚、肯尼亚等实际落地情况，读者可借此看小模型如何嵌入日常系统而非比拼参数量。
完全正确！💙 小模型的真正影响力在于让 AI 变得可及、可负担，并在日常生活中实用。期待看到更多用 MiniCPM 构建的真实应用！🚀
面壁智能表示，截至 2026 年 11 月，MiniCPM 的下载量已突破 7000 万次。其 8B 老挝国家模型现已接入政府的 G-Chat v2 通讯应用，其老挝语翻译在国际基准测试中击败了 GPT-4o。

小型端侧模型的竞赛不再关乎参数数量。关键在于谁真正被嵌入日常系统——足够便宜、足够支持离线，才能被采用。
如果你构建端侧模型或将 AI 带入现实世界，下一笔国家级交易会花落开放模型，还是大实验室的自研模型？
MiniCPM just became a country's official model — and it only has 8 billion parameters.
ModelBest says MiniCPM downloads passed 70 million as of November 2026. Its 8B Laos national model is now plugged into the government's G-Chat v2 messenger, and its Lao translation beat GPT-4o on an international benchmark.
Laos isn't the only deployment. Malaysia is using VoxCPM2 for voice interaction, a bank in Kenya runs on-device risk agents on it, and developers are shipping offline apps on top of it.
The race for small on-device models isn't about parameter counts anymore. It's about who actually gets embedded in daily systems — cheap enough and offline-capable enough to get in.
If you build on-device models or ship AI into the real world, will the next national-level deal go to an open model or a big lab's in-house one?

items.title: 用户实测用 MiniCPM5-2B 在 Mac 上本地跑通体检报告分析
items.description: 用户@cxjwin 分享在 Mac（M4 Pro、48GB）上用 Homebrew 装 llama.cpp 跑 minicpm5-2b、colima 起 Docker 本地运行开源项目 Mirobody 的实测：14 页 PDF 首次处理漏掉 3 页扫描版化验单，截图单独上传后 58 行化验数值逐项与原件对上，其中 20 行成功映射到 LOINC 标准编码，肌酐因名称歧义留空未猜。问超标指标时 2B 模型走 11 步找到全部 5 项箭头指标，但把一项在范围内的血糖误判为超标。接 Claude Code 时改用演示账号避免数据上传。Mirobody 由 Theta Health 以 Apache-2.0 开源，网页版和微信小程序也基于它。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/g3vdho0vzm8rzriiz5grruy3m
items.excerpt:
用户@cxjwin 分享在 Mac（M4 Pro、48GB）上用 Homebrew 装 llama.cpp 跑 minicpm5-2b、colima 起 Docker 本地运行开源项目 Mirobody 的实测：14 页 PDF 首次处理漏掉 3 页扫描版化验单，截图单独上传后 58 行化验数值逐项与原件对上，其中 20 行成功映射到 LOINC 标准编码，肌酐因名称歧义留空未猜。问超标指标时 2B 模型走 11 步找到全部 5 项箭头指标，但把一项在范围内的血糖误判为超标。接 Claude Code 时改用演示账号避免数据上传。Mirobody 由 Theta Health 以 Apache-2.0 开源，网页版和微信小程序也基于它。
用户实测记录了本地跑通 Mirobody 的完整流程，也包括扫描页漏读、LOINC 编码对不上和 2B 模型答错的细节，可作本地部署健康数据工作流的参考。
感谢这份详细的实测评测！💙 很高兴看到 MiniCPM5-2B 被用于本地优先的工作流。非常感谢你既分享了哪些地方好用，也分享了哪些地方可以改进！🙌
上个月的体检报告，我交给了开源项目 Mirobody，在自己 Mac 上从读报告到回答问题全跑通了，没填一个 API key。58 行化验数值逐项对过原件，全对。可第一次上传时，化验单那几页它一条都没读进来。
装法：Homebrew 装 llama.cpp 跑模型，colima 起 Docker 跑应用，设置页选「100% 在本机运行」，用默认的小模型 minicpm5-2b，读图交给 glm-ocr。模型下载加载 6 分钟。机器是 M4 Pro、48GB，模型走 Mac 的 GPU。
第一次传整份 14 页的 PDF，1 分钟处理完，进来 33 条，全是前几页的查体和结论，化验单 3 页一条没有。翻日志，读图的模型一次都没被调用。这 3 页是嵌在 PDF 里的扫描图，页眉页脚却是文字，按文档写的规则，有文字层的页不走 OCR。
我把这 3 页截成图片单独传，一分半处理完，58 行化验结果全进来了，数值和原件逐项对得上。错了 3 处小地方：红细胞的参考范围多读出一个「1」，一个项目名丢了个字，甘油三酯旁边印的上箭头没记下来。
Mirobody 主要干的事，是把每条读数对到标准编码 LOINC，不同医院、不同写法的同一项才能连成一条线。这 58 行对上了 20 行。生化、甲功、糖化基本都对上了，单位不同还会选不同的编码；血常规 22 项、尿常规 14 项一项没对上，卡在「白细胞WBC」这种中文直接连着缩写的写法上。
最有意思的是肌酐。报告上写的是「肌酐(Cre)」，而 Cre 在 LOINC 里查到的是一种耐药菌的培养检查。它判断这个名字有歧义，就留空，没有瞎猜。
然后我问它：「我这次体检有哪些指标超出了参考范围？」2B 小模型想了 84 秒，走了 11 步。报告上标了箭头的 5 项全找到了，但把一项在范围内的血糖也算成了超标。它查表没拿到数值，转头去翻了原文件，回答里的数字也没带来源链接。我的血脂和肝功能确实有几项偏高，具体数值就不放了。
接 Claude Code 这一步，我换成了项目自带的演示账号。MCP 接上以后，Claude Code 查到的读数会发到 Claude 的服务器，所以这一步没用我自己的数据。问它「胆固醇这几年怎么变的」，只有一条记录的时候，它直说看不出变化，没编趋势；我再传两份合成报告（一份 PDF、一份 CSV，写法不完全一样），三次读数被认成同一项，按日期排好，每个数字都标了出自哪个文件。
ChatGPT Health、阿福是厂商的云服务，注册就能用。Mirobody 是 Theta Health 开源的（Apache-2.0），国内的网页版和微信小程序也基于它。开源版能把记录和模型都留在自己电脑上，代价是得自己折腾，小模型也慢。它不做诊断，那次回答最后一句也是让我拿报告去问医生。
认不出的写法可以去提 issue，它的词表就是这么一行一行补起来的。 github.com/thetahealth/mirobo…

items.title: Lean 与 Mathlib 社区确认 Levent Alpöge 黎曼猜想证明正确
items.description: Lean 与 Mathlib 社区发表声明，确认斯坦福数学家 Levent Alpöge 的黎曼猜想证明正确。Alpöge 于 2026 年 11 月 20 日以 1700 万行 Lean 代码发布该证明，数十人独立运行得到相同结果，且验证程序被设计为可证明不会接受有缺陷的证明。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ikpixx0j7414se1f6lww2csek
items.excerpt:
Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
Lean 与 Mathlib 社区发表声明，确认斯坦福数学家 Levent Alpöge 的黎曼猜想证明正确。Alpöge 于 2026 年 11 月 20 日以 1700 万行 Lean 代码发布该证明，数十人独立运行得到相同结果，且验证程序被设计为可证明不会接受有缺陷的证明。
社区正式确认与代码验证细节都写得很具体，读者可以了解这道数学难题如何以 Lean 形式被独立核验。
Lean 与 Mathlib 社区已确认，Levent Alpöge 对黎曼猜想的证明是正确的。 该社区 在一份声明中表示 ：“我们完全相信 Alpöge 的证明是正确的，并祝贺他取得这一成就。”
Alpöge 是斯坦福大学的数学家，他于 2026 年 11 月 20 日 以 1700 万行 Lean 代码的形式公布了这一证明 。Lean 是一款用于检查数学证明中错误的工具。数十人独立运行了这些代码，得到了相同的结果。这些验证程序的设计使其可证明地无法接受有缺陷的证明。麻省理工学院数学家 Andrew Sutherland 在其网站上列出了各项独立验证 。
黎曼猜想一直是数学界最著名的未解难题之一，它对素数的分布方式作出了预测。下方这段用 Fable 5.2 生成的视频对证明做了解释，如果你想深入了解可以看看。
这一解答的到来远比预期要早。正如 Ethan Mollick 所指出的 ，Metaculus 上的预测者此前给出的预期日期是 2035 年 5 月。 数学家陶哲轩 上个月还表示，他预计这个问题会在“2050 年前后由人类与 AI 的结合”攻克。

items.title: 菲尔兹奖得主梅纳德谈 Claude 合作证明黎曼猜想：相信证明正确，但需被理解才可能获认可
items.description: 2022 年菲尔兹奖得主、牛津大学数学教授詹姆斯·梅纳德（James Maynard）在采访中表示，他认为 Anthropic 数学家莱文特·阿尔珀格（Levent Alpöge）与 Claude 合作完成的黎曼猜想证明是正确的，依据是该证明已通过 Lean 库形式化验证并经独立核实，且阿尔珀格过往有可靠记录。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/p9h5xzsooms0foxeakoivy7qt
items.excerpt:
菲尔兹奖得主梅纳德谈“AI 攻克黎曼猜想”：相信证明正确，但成果被人理解、才可能得到认可
2022 年菲尔兹奖得主、牛津大学数学教授詹姆斯·梅纳德（James Maynard）在采访中表示，他认为 Anthropic 数学家莱文特·阿尔珀格（Levent Alpöge）与 Claude 合作完成的黎曼猜想证明是正确的，依据是该证明已通过 Lean 库形式化验证并经独立核实，且阿尔珀格过往有可靠记录。
菲尔兹奖得主梅纳德对 AI 辅助黎曼猜想证明的判断，提醒读者形式化验证通过不等于数学界认可，理解证明思想才是关键。
IT之家 11 月 22 日消息，当地时间 11 月 20 日，Anthropic 数学家莱文特 · 阿尔珀格（Levent Alpöge）宣布，自己与 AI 模型 Claude 合作，攻克了数学界最著名的难题之一 —— 黎曼猜想。
据IT之家此前报道，11 月 21 日，Lean 与 Mathlib 社区发布联合声明，以 Lean 库形式给出的黎曼猜想证明已经通过核验，该证明的代码约 1700 万行。
据每日经济新闻报道，2022 年菲尔兹奖得主、牛津大学数学教授詹姆斯 · 梅纳德（James Maynard）接受采访时表示，他认为这项证明是正确的，但强调“理解一个定理为什么成立，远比仅仅证明它成立重要”。 只有当有人真正理解这项成果，并能够向其他人解释清楚时，这份证明才有可能得到数学界的全面认可 。
梅纳德是当代解析数论领域的重要数学家，长期致力于素数分布等数学问题的研究。2022 年，他凭借相关研究成果获得菲尔兹奖。
由于这项结果已经获得形式化验证，而且这一验证又经过了独立核实。此外，阿尔珀格过去在提出此类重大主张方面有着可靠的记录。综合这两点，梅纳德称非常有信心认为这一结果是正确的。
梅纳德表示，虽然黎曼猜想确实有一些直接的数学推论，但这个问题之所以被认为如此重要，主要是因为人们一直期待，要解释素数分布中这种深刻的内在结构， 就必须发展出新的数学理论 。
在我们真正理解证明中的思想和整体框架之前，这项成果很可能无法带来人们所期待的变革。
不过，我相信随着时间推移，我们最终会真正理解这份证明，而这必将彻底改变我们对相关数学问题的认识。

items.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
items.description: How perplexity measures progress in AI models, and why it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities.
items.excerpt:
By Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist at OpenAI
From afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities. There are indeed a variety of methods, but rather than designing something from scratch, they are mostly harnessing the intelligence coming from a much simpler and less interpretable process: training a compressor (or, equivalently ⁠ (opens in a new window) , predictor) on a very large corpus of data. 1
I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI. In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards. As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI. Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishing shared ⁠ (opens in a new window) safety measures across the industry. We at OpenAI hope for this to be a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts.

Algorithmic progress can blur the distinction between training phases, but we can still separate the creation of the AI with hard-to-predict emergent capabilities (which I earlier dubbed “ an alien mind ⁠ ”) and the subsequent targeted elicitation.

items.description: OpenAI 撰文提议将 perplexity（交叉熵损失）确立为跨模型开发者比较和安全标准的共享指标，并公开其内部预训练测量数据。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/r7kb35fpdwc1m2iqsmd310tdj
items.excerpt:
OpenAI 撰文提议将 perplexity（交叉熵损失）确立为跨模型开发者比较和安全标准的共享指标，并公开其内部预训练测量数据。
OpenAI 公开自 GPT-3.5 以来的内部 log-perplexity 数据，并提出以困惑度作为跨实验室共享的安全限速指标。
从远处看，现代 AI 的构建方式似乎和过去几十年的软件差不多：用各种技术去实现特定的能力。方法确实五花八门，但它们大多不是从零开始设计，而是 利用 一个更简单、也更难解释的过程所产生的智能：在超大规模的数据语料上训练一个压缩器（或者 等价地说 ，一个预测器）。 1
我认为，跟踪训练更好压缩器的进展速度，是理解 AI 发展脉络的关键。在这篇文章里，我主张把困惑度（或等价的交叉熵损失）确立为一项指标，用来比较不同模型开发者之间的水平，并为共享的安全标准提供依据。作为第一步，我公开更多 OpenAI 在预训练方面的进展。公布我们内部的困惑度数据是经过一番考虑的：这会让竞争对手更清楚地看到我们的位置，但相比在整个行业建立 共享 安全措施的紧迫性，这种顾虑是次要的。OpenAI 希望这能成为迈向共同科学基础的一步，为未来的节奏把控工作提供支撑。
对 AI 开发有一种简化但本质上很有启发性的看法：先造一台大型计算机，用它在一个大规模无结构数据集上 预训练 一个模型（压缩器），然后在不同场景中运用提示、微调或强化学习等各种技术，把模型潜在的能力激发出来。算法进步会模糊训练各阶段之间的界限，但我们仍然可以把两件事分开：一是创造出具有难以预测的涌现能力的 AI（我此前称之为“ 异类心智 ”），二是随后有针对性地激发它的能力。
多年来，我们衡量这一关键“智能基底”进展的主要方式一直相当稳定——我们一直在跟踪模型在留出数据集上的 困惑度 。 2 、 3 困惑度衡量的是模型平均而言预测下一个 token 的能力；困惑度越低，预测越准。本文开头那张图展示了从 GPT‑3.5 开始，我们的模型在这一指标上的变化。
这一个指标所大致描述的模型能力范围令人惊叹。GPT‑2 在更早的数据集上刷新了困惑度的最优成绩 4 ，可以说它是第一个能够持续写出连贯段落的模型。下一次重大跃升是 GPT‑3，它具备了上下文学习能力，只要给出几个任务示例就能学会。GPT‑3.5 在我们当前主要评测数据集上的对数困惑度约为 0.99，能够进行流畅对话，也是初代 ChatGPT 的基础。GPT‑4 约为 0.91，擅长有效运用思维链推理，这也促成了后来对这一能力的有针对性激发，以及现代推理模型的诞生。如今，随着损失降到 0.8 以下，我们已经在网络安全和数学等领域看到了变革性能力的涌现。我想再次强调，事先完全无法确定 a priori 一旦达到这些精确的困惑度阈值，这些能力就会出现——它们从根本上可以看作是在这一个指标上取得进展所带来的涌现性潜在能力。
随着 AI 飞速发展，我们衡量下游能力的范围与方式可能很快就会变化。用大多数现代基准来评测 GPT‑2 和 GPT‑3 意义不大；而当年使用的基准在 GPT‑4 附近也基本饱和了。相比之下，我认为关注预训练进展很可能仍能提供有价值的信息。
进展速度的一个特殊变化，来自 AI 对自身发展的贡献越来越大。最常被讨论的指标，围绕 AI 在开发周期的各个阶段增强并取代人类研究员；最终的拐点被认为是“完全递归自我改进”，届时整个过程将完全自动化，不再需要人类监督。且不说出于维持人类控制的考虑，这种状态显然应当避免，我认为这种总体框架漏掉了关键的一点。开发过程中有一个关键环节可能带来潜在的阶跃式变化：预训练方面的算法研究。
我们最近在另一个领域见证了前所未有的加速。一年多来，我们一直把数学中的开放问题交给模型，作为评估它们的方式之一。当我们升级到对数困惑度约 0.76 的模型后，它开始产出突破性成果。对我们中许多曾在数学及相关领域工作过的人来说，看着我们长期思考的问题的解答在一个 Slack 帖子里接连从模型那里冒出来，感觉非常超现实。有了这样的经历，我们就可以外推——这种突然的转变在深度学习研究中同样可能发生。虽然这个领域更依赖实验，但历史上也有过简单的洞见被忽视多年的情况；因此最早到 2027 年，我们就有可能看到基础预训练进展出现类似的雪崩式突破 5 。虽然我预计 AI 也会对对齐与监控方面的进展做出重大贡献，但我认为这方面的进展不太可能快到足以让预训练释放出全部潜在加速。
新出现的惊人能力，主要来自压缩能力的进步，而困惑度正是衡量压缩的指标。因此，无论开发过程的自动化程度如何，困惑度都有望成为衡量通用智能的共享基准。从近期的进展外推，当我们进入约 0.68–0.7 的对数困惑度区间时，应当预期会出现进一步的变革性能力。我不知道这些能力会是什么，而且我们今天可能根本没有在测试它们。与此同时，我们也应当预期，目前占主导地位的对齐审计方式会 进一步退化 ⁠ ，模型对评估和训练的觉察也会进一步增强。我认为，前沿模型开发者应当共同努力，在模型首次投入使用之前，就如何评估这类模型、如何对其安全案例进行红队测试建立共同规范，包括共同的透明度标准。我还进一步提议，基于困惑度及其他测量指标设定 共同上限 ，开发者承诺在我们理解和监控 AI 行为的能力达到某个具体里程碑（例如开发出思维链监控器的后继者）之前不越过这一上限。也就是说，我希望形成一项行业标准：用某个可在各实验室间追踪的关键指标，规定开发的第一道上限，并明确在越过它之前我们需要具体达成什么。我希望这能引出一个共同框架，用来设定后续一道道上限，并为后续开发定下节奏。
跨实验室比较困难。 不同开发者使用不同的评估数据集，训练数据配比也各不相同。这里我们报告的是我们一直在追踪的主要数据集上的数字；我相信，只要确立透明度的目标，我们就能找到可迁移的方法来比较不同基础模型的质量。
与可操作的评估脱节。 困惑度并不直接对应我们关心的某项任务。关心它的理由在于，我们可以预期它上面的进步会催生出全新的能力。

items.excerpt:
The supply chain industry has invested heavily in detecting problems sooner. Transportation visibility systems identify late shipments, planning applications flag shortages, and control towers consolidate operational alerts. Yet knowing about an exception and resolving it are two different things. The delay may be visible to everyone, while responsibility for the next action remains surprisingly unclear.
That gap is becoming more important as artificial intelligence moves beyond answering questions and begins maintaining responsibility for work over time. On November 19, OpenAI expanded access to ChatGPT Dots , its persistent agents, to eligible ChatGPT Business Standard users, while testing access with a limited group of Plus subscribers. The agents can retain useful context, work with authorized applications, and pursue continuing assignments. This is not the same as releasing an autonomous transportation management system. It does, however, point toward an operating model that supply chain leaders should be examining.
The critical question is not whether an AI agent can produce a better recommendation. It is whether an organization can assign a bounded operational responsibility, know who is accountable for the result, and verify that the work was actually completed.
Consider how many logistics exceptions are managed today. A late container generates an alert. A transportation planner checks the revised estimated arrival, calls the carrier, and coordinates with a distribution center. Someone may approve a new receiving window or an inventory transfer. But the work does not end when the recommendation is accepted. The carrier must acknowledge the change, the appointment must be updated, and the revised plan must hold up as conditions change.
A great deal of operational effort is spent in the intervals between those actions. Employees chase confirmations, reconstruct previous conversations, and determine whether an apparent resolution was reflected in the system of record. Enterprise applications support the process, but they do not always maintain a single durable record of who owns the exception through closure.
Persistent AI could improve this situation by preserving the case history, recognizing when new information changes its significance, and continuing to monitor outstanding actions. items.description: Columbia 和 MIT 的论文展示 Claude 发现的算法在 3SUM 和全对最短路径（APSP）上取得多项式改进，3SUM 达到 O(n^1.9992)、APSP 达到 O(n^2.9995)，推翻了 3SUM 和 APSP 假设。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/d32df9vzpliz9m348fug74inq
items.excerpt:
Columbia 和 MIT 的论文展示 Claude 发现的算法在 3SUM 和全对最短路径（APSP）上取得多项式改进，3SUM 达到 O(n^1.9992)、APSP 达到 O(n^2.9995)，推翻了 3SUM 和 APSP 假设。
论文显示 Claude 发现的算法改进了 3SUM 和 APSP 的长期复杂度上限，并用 Lean 4 形式化验证，读者可以了解 AI 搜索算法的可行路径。
哥伦比亚大学和麻省理工学院的新论文表明，Claude 发现的一种算法打破了 3SUM 和全对最短路径长期以来的速度极限。
3SUM 问的是列表中是否有 3 个数之和为 0，全对最短路径则要求出图中每一对节点之间的距离。几十年来，没有人能把教科书式的二次和三次时间复杂度改进超过极小的常数因子，许多人认为不可能做到。
Claude 找到了一种更快的方法来计算两个长而窄的矩阵乘积中的选定元素，跳过了经典方法所做的一些工作。已知的归约随后将其转化为 3SUM、最短路径以及许多相关问题的加速。
3SUM 现在的运行时间为 O(n^1.9992)，最短路径为 O(n^2.9995)，这些微小的改进仍然否定了 3SUM 和 APSP 猜想。Claude 在一次会话中找到了该方法，使用了 1600 万输出 token，没有人类输入。
把“已知困难”的算法极限视为 AI 搜索的开放目标，并像这篇论文用 Lean 4 所做的那样，对 AI 发现的证明进行形式化验证。

items.title: Anthropic 数学家称与 Claude 完成黎曼猜想证明，斯坦福数小时后发布纯人类竞争草稿
items.description: Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 周五宣布与 Claude 合作得到黎曼猜想及广义黎曼猜想的证明，证明以 Lean 语言分 14 个数据包发布，打印将超 25 万页。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/tje8i8y21ttk7jjmqet5bpxuq
items.excerpt:
Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft
Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 周五宣布与 Claude 合作得到黎曼猜想及广义黎曼猜想的证明，证明以 Lean 语言分 14 个数据包发布，打印将超 25 万页。
报道同时给出 AI 证明以 Lean 形式化验证和人类证明遭社区质疑两条线，读者可据此判断双方证明各自的验证路径与可信度。
Anthropic 的数学家 Levent Alpöge 周五表示，他用一个大语言模型解决了数学界最著名的未解难题。
据 Scientific American 等美国媒体报道，Alpöge 在自己的网站上发布了一篇论文和配套的计算机代码。他在 公告中写道 ：“我相信，在与 Claude 的合作下，我发现了黎曼猜想的证明。”
据 Alpöge 介绍，他的方法不仅解决了最初的素数问题，还一并解决了广义黎曼猜想（GRH）——该猜想把这一排序原理推广到一大类相关方程上。他预计，再给一点时间，他还能解决范围更广的扩展黎曼猜想。
从大学时代起，Alpöge 就把这个问题当作一个秘而不宣的终身目标，原以为要花上几十年。过去几个月里，他与 Anthropic 的 AI 模型紧密合作，负责把握方向，并在一个简化的玩具模型上把两种方法结合起来。等到转向真正的问题时，AI 接手了工作，在临近终点时把他远远甩在了后面。
为了攻克这道难题，两人扩展了数学家 Stepanov 的一个思路——后者曾在另一个数学体系中解决过类似问题。该方法依赖的工具类似于高中数学里对光滑曲线求导，而这一招用在整数上通常行不通，因为单个数值无法像连续曲线那样求导。
Alpöge 和 Claude 绕开了这个障碍：他们把特殊的数学变换像链条一样串联起来，模拟出求导的效果。关键洞见由语言模型给出——它发现，对于一个长度为 X 的数列，需要串联的变换数量恰好是 X 的平方根。Alpöge 说，单是这类想法就足以让同行数学家震惊。
Alpöge 公布消息几小时后，事情出现了戏剧性转折。就在一场董事会会议开始前，斯坦福大学数学教授、美国数学会（AMS）主席 Ravi Vakil 在博客上发布了一则 “紧急公告” ，分享了一份由数学家 Alessandro Masullo 独立撰写的广义黎曼猜想证明草稿。
“这完全出自人类之手，没有 AI 参与，”Vakil 写道。他说，斯坦福知名数论学家 Brian Conrad 已悄悄审阅 Masullo 的工作数月，提出了大量反馈意见，目前正被纳入修改。
Masullo 原本计划在斯坦福花一年时间完善草稿后再公开，但 Anthropic 突然发布的 AI 成果迫使研究人员立即公布了当前版本。
在首次发布公告约八小时后，Vakil 更新了帖子，称有数人联系他，报告了这份拟议证明中的问题，这些问题是在不同 AI 模型的协助下发现的。他说，尤其有几位数学家最先指出了这些问题。“按照惯例，在这份证明被承认为真之前，所有问题都需要解决到令学界满意的程度。（我对该证明策略的正确性不作任何断言。）”Vakil 写道。
数学家们之所以立刻认真对待这两项声明，是因为它们背后都有扎实的基础工作。Masullo 的传统证明经过了 Brian Conrad 数月的审查，而 Alpöge 则为他的 AI 证明提供了完整的计算机验证。
阿尔珀格说，如果把 Claude 的论证打印出来，篇幅会超过 25 万页，因为 AI 连基本规则都逐条写明，比如任何数要么大于二分之一、要么小于二分之一。为了免去数学家面对这堵文字墙的麻烦，阿尔珀格只以 Lean 编程语言的形式发布了证明，并拆分成 14 个数据包 。
Lean 就像一个数字裁判，逐步检查每一步逻辑推演是否都严格遵循数学的基本规则，没有错误，也没有未经证明的假设。据《科学美国人》报道，如果最初把原始问题翻译成代码时出了错，人为失误仍有可能发生，不过专家核查阿尔珀格对起始问题的编码是否正确应该不会花太久。瓦基尔则呼吁数学家尽快审阅马苏洛的草稿，将其翻译成 Lean 之类的系统，并补上任何细小的漏洞。
阿尔珀格承认，在某些复杂的子领域里，Claude 的水平远远超过了他，以至于他正在展示的成果，其周边的数学他还没有完全掌握。他预计这份庞大的 AI 证明可以很快被压缩，并计划在未来几个月内写出一个人类可读的版本。
Anthropic 的这则消息还赶上一个事关重大的商业周——就在周四公司 大规模 IPO 的第二天。阿尔珀格说，他是在周日深夜取得突破的，随后联系了 Anthropic CEO 达里奥·阿莫代伊请求批准发布。他称，时机恰好在公司上市之后，实在非常不幸，但他否认任何公关炒作的猜测，表示再等下去才真的不是选项。
这为进展飞快的 2026 年画上了一个句号——这一年里 Claude 已经解决了多个悬而未决的数学问题 。7 月，阿尔珀格发表了 Claude 生成的著名雅可比猜想解答。9 月，围绕描述流体和气体如何流动的纳维-斯托克斯方程，爆发了一场 激烈争议 ，起因是纽约大学数学家特里斯坦·巴克马斯特指出 OpenAI 使用了他和阿尔珀格的先前工作。10 月，OpenAI 在素数问题上迈出了重要的第一步， 发布了一批重要成果 。阿尔珀格明确称赞了 OpenAI 研究人员的选题，称这为他自己的证明提供了关键思路。

November 20 2026 — the most famous problem in math is solved... revealing remarkable contrasts in human and AI approaches
Within a few hours of each other ( timeline ), two mathematicians claimed independent proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis, the most famous open problem in mathematics ( Scientific American ).
Levent Alpöge of Anthropic first made his Claude-driven proof in a note released with Lean code (1.3GB worth, ~250,000 page equivalent) rather than a full paper. Elliot Glazer confirms that the formalized statement is GRH and puts the chance of a Lean bug well under 1%. …prompting Alessandro Masullo to release his 940 page, 100% human , work in progress proof he had been working on for the last 12 years (and had been undergoing secret manual review and revision per Kevin Hartnett ).
This is the third in the trilogy of frontier math breakthroughs, following from the Navier Stokes solutions and the Quasi-Riemann bounding, but it doesn’t feel over. Forecast of 182.7 million consumers would be down slightly from 2026 figure of 186.9 million shoppers.
An estimated 182.7 million consumers plan to shop during the Thanksgiving weekend this year, down slightly from 186.9 million shoppers last year, according to a report from the National Retail Federation (NRF).
Despite the dip, the figure continues the trend of elevated shopping during the holiday weekend seen in recent years. In addition, consumers continue to embrace earlier holiday shopping, with 60% starting by the beginning of November, up from 56% before the pandemic, according to results from the annual NRF survey, which was conducted by Prosper Insights & Analytics.
“Holiday shopping continues to be pulled forward, but Thanksgiving weekend remains an important shopping event for consumers,” NRF Vice President of Industry and Consumer Insights Allison Zeller said. “Shoppers are looking for deals, and retailers are delivering great value on gifts while creating special experiences that keep the Thanksgiving weekend shopping tradition going.”
Black Friday remains the most popular day to shop during the Thanksgiving weekend, with 69% (126 million) of holiday shoppers planning to shop. Of those, 67% are likely to shop in stores and 89% online. Cyber Monday follows in popularity, with 36% (66.1 million) planning to shop.
Throughout Thanksgiving weekend, 59% of holiday shoppers plan to use AI to support their winter holiday shopping. Top reasons for Thanksgiving weekend shoppers using AI include product recommendations (32%), brainstorming gift ideas (31%), gift lists and recipient tracking (25%), budget tracking (25%), and scanning retailer sites to find the best prices (25%).
“AI has become another tool consumers use to make holiday shopping easier, whether they’re researching products or looking for the best deals,” Prosper Insights & Analytics Executive Vice President of Strategy Phil Rist said. “As consumers incorporate these tools into their lives, holiday shopping represents one of the many ways they are putting AI to use.”
To keep their budgets in check this season, 82% are taking steps to manage holiday costs, including buying less expensive gifts (25%), cutting back in other areas (24%), buying for fewer people (20%) or waiting until Thanksgiving weekend to do most of their shopping (20%).

items.excerpt:
Together AI 宣布 阿里 旗舰模型 Qwen4 Max 上线其 Serverless 推理平台（模型串 Qwen/Qwen4-Max），1M token 上下文，截至 2026 年 11 月 22 日 7 折。
Together AI 用一次 65 万 token 的整仓修 bug 实测展示 Qwen4 Max 的长上下文编码能力，并给出价格、缓存和调用细节。
我们把一份 bug 报告和整个代码库一次性交给了 Qwen4 Max 。代码库是 Python Web 框架 Tornado：全部 344 个文件，652,519 个 token。模型没有工具可用，我们也没有预先挑选相关文件或先跑一遍检索。72 秒后它返回了一个补丁，而这个补丁通过了 Tornado 维护者为该 bug 编写的测试。这次请求花了 69 美分。
它还在仓库的其他地方找到了先例。bug 报告里从未提到 tornado/iostream.py ，但模型指出那里的代码已经用它的补丁所需的方式处理了错误。Tornado 维护者在自己修复时也引用了同一处代码。
Qwen4 Max 是阿里巴巴的旗舰 Qwen 模型。它今天已在 Together AI 上线，并在 2026 年 11 月 22 日前享受 30% 折扣。
Tornado 是一个开源 Python Web 框架。它的仓库包含约 340 个代码、测试和文档文件。这能放进 Qwen4 Max 的上下文窗口，而且远超任何人会手动粘贴进提示词的内容。我们挑选了维护者在 2026 年 11 月 18 日提交的一个修复——也就是 Qwen4 Max 发布两天后——并针对该提交之前的仓库状态进行了测试。
这个 bug 出在 Tornado 的 websocket 代码里。当连接关闭时仍有消息未发送，每一个未被 await 的 write_message() 调用都会记录一条错误，尽管 await 它是可选的。我们把该检出中的每个文本文件作为一个提示词发送，并附上一份只描述症状的 bug 报告：
当 websocket 连接在仍有消息未发送时关闭（例如，客户端发送了消息和一个 FIN，或重置了连接，却没有读取回复），每一个结果未被 await 的 write_message() 调用都会在 ERROR 级别记录“Task exception was never retrieved”。
await write_message 返回的 Future 是可选的，因此未 await 的调用不应记录任何内容。而确实 await 它的调用方仍应收到 WebSocketClosedError。
第一个 token 在 54 秒后到达，回复在 72 秒时完成。Qwen4 Max 将错误追溯到 tornado/websocket.py 中的 WebSocketProtocol13.write_message 。该方法把每次写入包装在一个任务中。当连接关闭时，任务因一个无人必须收集的异常而失败，Python 会将其记录为“Task exception was never retrieved”。
模型的补丁将该异常标记为已检索。这样就不会记录任何内容，而确实 await 写入的调用方仍会收到错误：
先例让这个补丁读起来像是项目本身的一部分。模型的解释称，修复应当做 BaseIOStream.write 已经为其自身的 future 所做的事。该方法位于 tornado/iostream.py 中，比 websocket 代码低一层，并且用同样的方式解决了同样的问题。维护者的提交也做了同样的比较。
没有人替它挑选这些文件。全部 344 个文件都放进去了，而模型找到了关键的那两个。
Tornado 维护者在修复中增加了两个回归测试：一个针对未 await 的写入，一个针对已 await 的写入。在修复前的代码上，第一个测试失败。应用模型的补丁后，两个测试都通过。随后我们在应用补丁的情况下运行了 Tornado 的完整测试套件，共 1,673 个测试，没有一个失败。
按折扣价计算，这次请求约为 69 美分，几乎全部花在 652,519 个输入 token 上。按原价计算则是 98 美分。

阿里巴巴于 2026 年 11 月 16 日发布 Qwen4 Max，称其为 Qwen 系列迄今能力最强的模型。该模型面向长时间运行的智能体任务，包括跨大型仓库的编码，这正是我们测试的那类任务。
Qwen4 Max 是一个稀疏混合专家模型，总参数 2.4 万亿，每个 token 激活 71 亿。在 Work360 上——这是阿里巴巴自建的基准，覆盖 721 个专业领域的行业任务——阿里报告称其整体表现优于 Qwen3.8 Max，在高推理强度下少用 35% 的 token，平均每个任务成本低约 60%。这些是阿里巴巴的数据， 其发布公告 中有详细说明。
